strengths: Addresses a well-motivated and practically important problem: enabling training-free video reasoning segmentation by probing intrinsic MLLM localization ability, avoiding costly LoRA/SAM co-training pipelines used by prior work.

Extensive empirical evaluation spanning three MLLM families (LLaVA-OV, InternVL3, Qwen2VL/2.5VL) and five datasets (three referring VOS, two reasoning VOS), which supports the generality claims better than a single-model, single-dataset study.

Thorough and honest reproducibility analysis of baselines: the paper carefully documents why Loc-Head's heuristics (bottom-row exclusion, RefCOCO-based head discovery) and TAM's token-dependence fail to generalize to the video/reasoning setting, lending credibility to the comparisons.

Comprehensive ablations (contrastive fusion, video-frame fusion, multi-scale complementing, rollout normalization, SAM prompting thresholds, consistency score design, MLLM scaling) that isolate the contribution of each proposed component and show consistent, non-trivial gains.

Achieves performance competitive with (and sometimes exceeding) training-based methods (VISA, VideoLISA, and close to GLUS/Veason-R1) despite requiring no fine-tuning, which is a meaningful practical result.
Includes candid failure-case analysis (thin/elongated objects, small transient objects, attention-consistency penalty edge cases), improving transparency about the method's limitations.
weaknesses: The pipeline is fairly complex and introduces many hand-tuned hyperparameters (τpq, τtrk, NMS IoU=0.7, rollout starting layer, Gaussian smoothing, Otsu vs. mean thresholding for s^ac) that are themselves heuristic choices, somewhat undercutting the paper's central critique of Loc-Head for relying on heuristics.

No analysis of computational cost/inference latency is provided; the method requires multiple additional forward passes per video (object-focused prompt, background-focused prompt, video-level and frame-level rollout, SAM2 point-prompt propagation), which could make it substantially slower than single-pass training-based approaches despite being 'training-free.'

Absolute performance of attention-only masks (Table 1) remains quite low (J&F often in the teens-to-twenties), and contour accuracy (F) is notably weaker than region similarity (J), indicating the core attention-based localization signal is still coarse and only becomes competitive after heavy SAM2 post-processing.

The optimal starting layer for rollout and threshold values vary by model/dataset (Table 5b, Table 6), suggesting some residual model-specific tuning is still needed despite claims of a unified, model-agnostic framework.
Limited evaluation of multi-object scenarios beyond qualitative examples; no dedicated quantitative benchmark or metric specifically targeting multi-object disambiguation performance.

Technical novelty is somewhat incremental: individual components (attention rollout, contrastive prompting, multi-scale fusion, SAM-guided prompting) are combinations/adaptations of existing ideas rather than fundamentally new mechanisms, and the primary contribution is largely engineering/empirical rather than conceptual.

Only 16 uniformly sampled frames are used in main experiments; there is no analysis of sensitivity to frame sampling density or performance on longer videos, which limits confidence in scalability claims.

strengths: Extensive empirical validation across three MLLM families (LLaVA-OV, InternVL3, Qwen2/2.5VL) and five datasets (referring and reasoning VOS), with consistent improvements over training-free baselines (Loc-Head, TAM) and performance competitive with or exceeding several training-based methods, which is a notable result for a purely training-free pipeline.

Clear, well-motivated decomposition of the problem into two intuitive fusion mechanisms (contrastive object-background and complementary video-frame), each independently ablated and shown to contribute meaningfully to performance (Tables 4-5).

Thorough ablation studies covering rollout normalization, layer selection, SAM prompting thresholds, and the attention consistency scoring mechanism, indicating careful engineering and analysis of design choices.

Very extensive appendix with failure case analysis, prompt robustness studies (three prompt variants for each of the three prompt types), part-level segmentation exploration, non-explicit/implicit object expression cases, and detailed critique/reproduction analysis of baseline methods (Loc-Head, TAM), which strengthens confidence in the reported comparisons and reproducibility.

The method is conceptually simple (rollout + subtraction + averaging + thresholding) and requires no additional training, making it broadly applicable and easy to adopt across different MLLM backbones.
weaknesses: Novelty is somewhat incremental: the core techniques (attention rollout, contrastive prompting for saliency, multi-scale fusion, point-prompting SAM) are each individually well-established; the contribution is primarily a careful combination and engineering of these existing ideas for a new task setting rather than a fundamentally new mechanism.

The pipeline is fairly complex and relies on many hand-tuned components and thresholds (τpq, τtrk, Gaussian smoothing, Otsu vs. mean thresholding, NMS overlap threshold, per-frame vs global normalization), raising concerns about how well these choices transfer to unseen domains beyond the tested benchmarks, despite the robustness ablations provided.

The method requires multiple separate MLLM forward passes per video (object-focused, background-focused, category-choice, video-level, and frame-level per-frame queries), which likely introduces significant computational/inference overhead compared to a single-pass captioning/QA baseline; this cost is not clearly quantified or compared against baselines.

Absolute performance on the more complex reasoning benchmarks (ReVOS, ReasonVOS) remains substantially lower than top training-based methods (e.g., Veason-R1, VRS-HQ) in several settings, and the paper's own results show clear degradation on challenging sub-cases like multiple similar objects, small/thin objects, and part-level segmentation (acknowledged in appendix), suggesting the practical robustness gains are still limited for hard cases.

The correctness of the whole contrastive fusion pipeline hinges on accurately inferring a single object category name from the expression, which may be fragile for expressions with multiple targets, ambiguous references, or when the query does not map cleanly to a single noun (e.g., non-explicit expressions rely on similar category inference)—the paper shows successful qualitative cases but does not quantify how often/why this step fails at scale.

Some baseline reproduction gaps are large and rely on the authors' own reimplementation and heuristics (e.g., Loc-Head's SAM prompting score dropping from 74.2 to 34.4 upon reproduction), which, while explained, makes exact quantitative comparisons somewhat dependent on the authors' interpretation of baseline settings.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated training-free approach that decomposes attention rollout into contrastive object-background and complementary video-frame fusion, directly addressing the visual attention sink problem identified in prior work.

Extensive experimental validation across three MLLM families (LLaVA-OV, InternVL3, Qwen2VL/2.5VL) and five datasets (three referring VOS, two reasoning VOS), demonstrating consistent improvements over training-free baselines (Loc-Head, TAM).

Strong empirical results: the method not only outperforms other training-free methods by large margins but also matches or surpasses several training-based methods (e.g., outperforms VISA/VideoLISA on Ref-DAVIS and MeViS, and surpasses all training-based methods including an RL-trained Veason-R1 on ReasonVOS) despite requiring no training.

Thorough ablation studies isolating the contribution of each component (object-background contrasting, video-frame complementing, multi-scale fusion, rollout normalization, SAM prompting thresholds, attention consistency scoring), providing clear evidence for design choices.

Very extensive and honest appendix analysis, including failure case discussion, prompt robustness studies (showing the method is not overly sensitive to prompt phrasing), detailed reproduction analysis of baselines (Loc-Head, TAM) revealing their brittleness, part-level segmentation exploration, non-explicit/world-knowledge expression cases, and similar-multiple-object scenario comparisons with VRS-HQ.

The proposed attention-guided SAM2 prompting pipeline with tracklet scoring is a useful, generalizable contribution beyond the core fusion idea, effectively converting coarse attention into fine-grained masks without training a mask decoder.
Clear writing and figures that effectively illustrate the two fusion mechanisms and the overall pipeline.
weaknesses: The method involves multiple heuristic components (Gaussian smoothing, Otsu thresholding, several hand-tuned thresholds τpq, τtrk, NMS IoU threshold) whose interactions and sensitivity across arbitrary new datasets/models beyond those tested are not fully characterized, despite the threshold ablation provided.

Despite improvements, the approach still requires multiple additional MLLM forward passes per video (object-focused, background-focused, video-level, and per-frame prompts), and the paper does not report the computational/latency overhead compared to a single QA pass or to training-based baselines, which is relevant for a 'training-free' selling point that could still be inference-heavy.

On some referring-only benchmarks with less reasoning complexity (e.g., MeViS, Ref-YouTube-VOS), the method still noticeably trails state-of-the-art training-based methods (VRS-HQ, GLUS), somewhat tempering the 'comparable to training-based methods' claim to mainly the reasoning-heavy benchmarks.

The reliance on a single dominant object category extracted via prompting (object category choice prompt) may still struggle in genuinely ambiguous multi-object or multi-category referring scenarios, similar in spirit to the single-object limitation criticized in Loc-Head, though the paper provides some mitigating analysis.

Contour accuracy (F) of raw attention masks remains substantially lower than region similarity (J), indicating persistent boundary-precision limitations that are only partially resolved by the SAM2 stage.
